report.summary: 4 findings reviewed: 2 confirmed (docstring claims, token count mismatch), 1 narrowed (budget error in canary), 1 needs-evidence (hash functions). Deliverables: verify hash function definitions, audit docstring claims, document token count differences, add budget error tracking.
risks: If _body_sha or _entry_sha are missing, verify_chain will crash; need to confirm they exist before any chain operations.
Docstring claims in render.py may be stale; misleading documentation could cause developer confusion.
Token count mismatch is intentional but may still cause confusion in reports; clear documentation needed.
Budget errors not reflected in canary exit code may mask lane unavailability; need to decide if this is by design.
todos: Search for 'def _body_sha' and 'def _entry_sha' in daedalus/council/bus.py; if missing, add them or fix imports.
Audit full render.py to verify all docstring claims have corresponding implementations.
Document the token count difference between slice.py and eval/harness.py in a comment or docstring.
Add budget error tracking to canary.py exit code if not already present.

items.title: Verify and fix hash functions _body_sha and _entry_sha in bus.py
items.why_now: If these functions are missing, verify_chain will crash at runtime, breaking the entire council bus. This is a critical dependency for all chain operations.

steps.do: Search for 'def _body_sha' and 'def _entry_sha' in daedalus/council/bus.py. If not found, check for imports from another module. If missing, implement them or import them from the correct location.

items.assumption: The functions may be defined later in bus.py or imported from a module not shown in the partial chunk.

items.title: Audit render.py docstring claims against actual implementation
items.why_now: The docstring makes specific behavioral claims (analyse_once, gate mode, reconciliation, etc.) that are unverified. If missing, documentation is misleading.

steps.do: Read the full daedalus/spine/render.py and verify each claim in the docstring: analyse_once, gate mode, reconciliation, stamp generation, snapshot handling, escaping.
steps.verified_by: Create a test that calls each claimed function and asserts expected behavior, or update docstring to match actual code.

items.assumption: The full render.py file is available and can be read; no assumption about its size.

items.title: Document token count denominator differences between slice.py and eval/harness.py
items.why_now: The difference is intentional but not documented in code, causing confusion when comparing reduction_pct values. Clear documentation or a unified method is needed.

steps.do: Add a comment or docstring in daedalus/structcore/slice.py and daedalus/eval/harness.py explaining the token count difference: slice.py uses index-scoped counts, harness.py uses as-fed-to-model counts with headers and truncation.
steps.verified_by: Run `python -c "from daedalus.structcore.slice import count_tokens; help(count_tokens)"` and verify the docstring includes the explanation.

steps.do: Add a comment or docstring in daedalus/eval/harness.py explaining the token count difference.
steps.verified_by: Run `python -c "from daedalus.eval.harness import _whole_repo_text; help(_whole_repo_text)"` and verify the docstring includes the explanation.

items.assumption: The difference is indeed intentional and not a bug; if it is a bug, the fix would be more complex.

items.title: Add budget error tracking to canary.py exit code
items.why_now: Currently, budget errors do not cause a non-zero exit code, so a lane unavailable due to budget constraints would pass the canary. This could mask real issues.

steps.do: Search for 'budget' or 'BudgetError' in daedalus/council/canary.py. If no handling exists, modify the exit_code logic to include budget errors as a failure condition.
steps.verified_by: Write a test that simulates a budget error and asserts non-zero exit code, then run `pytest tests/test_canary_livewire.py -x -k budget`

items.assumption: The design intent is to treat budget errors as failures; if not, this item may be rejected.
